characteristic_features: end-organ damage from eosinophil infiltration (cardiac  endomyocardial fibrosis; pulmonary; neurologic; skin; GI)

biomarkers.name: FIP1L1-PDGFRA fusion (cryptic 4q12 deletion)
biomarkers.type: fusion / RT-PCR / FISH for CHIC2 deletion
biomarkers.prevalence: Defining for the WHO/ICC entity 'myeloid/lymphoid neoplasm with eosinophilia and PDGFRA rearrangement'; FIP1L1-PDGFRA is the most common PDGFRA fusion
biomarkers.clinical_use: Exquisitely imatinib-sensitive; very low doses (for example 100 mg/day, and in some patients less frequent dosing for maintenance) are often sufficient, with frequent deep molecular remissions

biomarkers.name: FGFR1 rearrangements (8p11 myeloid/lymphoid neoplasm)
biomarkers.clinical_use: Aggressive; generally imatinib-resistant. FGFR inhibitors including pemigatinib have demonstrated activity

biomarkers.name: JAK2 fusions (PCM1-JAK2)
biomarkers.clinical_use: Associated with myeloid/lymphoid neoplasm with eosinophilia and JAK2 rearrangement; ruxolitinib has clinical activity in some cases

biomarkers.name: Clonality demonstration (cytogenetics or molecular)
biomarkers.clinical_use: Required to distinguish chronic eosinophilic leukemia, NOS from idiopathic hypereosinophilic syndrome (HES)

biomarkers.name: Serum tryptase, vitamin B12, IgE
biomarkers.clinical_use: Elevated tryptase and/or vitamin B12 may support a myeloid neoplasm, including PDGFRA-rearranged disease; elevated IgE may support lymphocyte-variant HES rather than CEL

histomorphological_subtype.primary_pattern: Sustained hypereosinophilia with morphologic and/or molecular evidence of clonality; marrow may show eosinophilic hyperplasia with left shift
variants: myeloid/lymphoid neoplasm with eosinophilia and PDGFRA rearrangement (most commonly FIP1L1-PDGFRA; distinct WHO/ICC entity, imatinib-sensitive)
histomorphological_subtype.grading: Not graded; molecular subtype drives management

tumor_microenvironment.immune_context: End-organ damage from eosinophil infiltration is the pathophysiology  cardiac endomyocardial fibrosis, pulmonary infiltrates, neuropathy, skin, GI
tumor_microenvironment.stromal_features: Marrow eosinophilic hyperplasia; end-organ eosinophilic infiltration causing tissue damage

cellular_states_and_lineage.cell_of_origin: HSC or myeloid progenitor with kinase-activating fusion driving eosinophil-lineage-biased proliferation
cellular_states_and_lineage.differentiation_state: Sustained hypereosinophilia with morphologic and/or molecular evidence of clonality; marrow eosinophilic hyperplasia with left shift
cellular_states_and_lineage.lineage_plasticity: Distinct fusion-driven entities: myeloid/lymphoid neoplasm with eosinophilia and PDGFRA rearrangement (most commonly FIP1L1-PDGFRA; imatinib-sensitive), PDGFRB-rearranged, FGFR1-rearranged (aggressive with lymphoid/myeloid mixed presentation), JAK2-rearranged  each with distinct clinical behaviour and targeted therapy implications
